name: 1954 US polio vaccine field trial
description: A large US field trial evaluated a polio vaccine in schoolchildren in 1954.

impact.note: One trial that confirmed an existing vaccine and released it for mass use in many countries, and became a model for later large field trials.

date.basis: Date refers to this scoped event or archaeological context, not to a global origin.

events.statement: A large US field trial evaluated a polio vaccine in schoolchildren in 1954.

evidence.supports: The historian reports 623,972 children in vaccine-or-placebo groups and over a million in observed-control groups in the 1954 US field trials, sponsored by the National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis. Trial designs differed; the count is not the number vaccinated or a population adoption rate.

events.caveats: The trial had different comparison designs. A 1955 manufacturing failure affected some batches after the field trials; the trial count is not the number vaccinated or community coverage.

events.statement: A serious manufacturing failure affected some vaccine batches during the subsequent 1955 rollout.

evidence.supports: CDC records that a serious manufacturing failure affected some vaccine batches in 1955 and prompted changes in oversight. The event followed the 1954 field trials and should not be attributed to all vaccine production.

events.caveats: The 1955 event was after the 1954 trial and did not involve all manufacturers.
